newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian navy completes rescue of Albanian ship.
newsitem.headline: Italian navy completes rescue of Albanian ship.

text.p: The Italian navy on Thursday completed a dramatic rescue operation to save an Albanian fishing boat packed with 350 refugees that was in danger of sinking in stormy seas off the coast of Albania, a spokesman said.
The operation lasted nearly 24 hours and was carried out in strong winds that had blown the ship to 14 miles off the Albanian coast.
The navy frigate Espero towed the boat to a calmer bay north of the Albanian port of Durres.
The refugees, who included 45 children, were then taken aboard landing craft to a beach in the Bay of Rodonit to be transferred by bus to Tirana and other destinations.
Other Italian navy and U.S. military ships were in the area to provide further assistance if needed.
"For us it was a great success because the boat risked sinking, had no fuel and the weather conditions were very bad," said Admiral Franco D'Agostino at Italian navy headquarters in Rome.

At the start of the rescue operation, seven people, most of them children, were winched off the boat by an Italian military helicopter before bad weather forced the aircraft to abandon further rescue attempts.
Navy officials also denied Italian media reports that Italian marines had landed in Albania to begin a humanitarian operation.
They said the reports had confused the rescue operation involving landing craft with government plans for a humanitarian mission which has not yet begun.
The boat ran into trouble about 40 miles from Durres, a main point of departure for more than 10,000 Albanians who have fled to Italy since March 13 after armed anarchy spread across the country.
They have crossed the Adriatic to southeastern Italian ports in a flotilla of rusting and ancient vessels, many of which Italian coastguards say are unseaworthy.
